title: Field Evidence Laminates — Sell Kit (rough)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, printable "laminate" kit for field sellers and SEs: a 6-card micro-deck (3 persona cards + 3 quick-proofs) that fits in a pocket wallet. Each card = 30–45s talking track + 1 proof + 1 quick counter for the top objection.

Why this exists (problem):
- Sellers need razor-fast, evidence-led responses during customer discovery and procurement conversations.
- Longer battlecards live in Notion/Drive and are ignored in the moment.
- We want consistent, measurable signals for the claims we make (latency, cost, fallback guarantees).

Audience / Personas (priority):
1) Integration / Platform Architect (cloud-native infra owners)
2) Product/ML Engineering Lead (ships features using inference)
3) Procurement / Finance (TCO-focused buyers)

Kit structure (physical or PDF flip):
- Card A1 (Architect): 20s hook + 30s proof + 10s snippet
  - Hook: "Keep inference predictable at scale — across hosted, dedicated, and private."
  - Proof: "3ms median token latency on chat paths in our hosted zone; Dedicated pools sustain 6k RPS for gpt-like workloads (customer X pilot)."
  - Top objection counter: "If you need strict isolation, Dedicated and Private options let you pin models and network boundaries — we do not co-tenant."

- Card P1 (ML Eng): 20s hook + 30s proof + 10s snippet
  - Hook: "Ship ML features faster without re-architecting your inference stack."
  - Proof: "Caching + continuous batching reduced per-token cost 28% on a customer RLHF chat flow; model variant fallbacks dropped error surface by 1.6x."
  - Counter: "We provide rollouts, A/B canary and automatic fallback by policy — you get predictable quality and the ability to test model changes safely."

- Card F1 (Procurement): 20s hook + 30s proof + 10s snippet
  - Hook: "Control spend with committed capacity or usage — pick the tradeoff that fits your forecast."
  - Proof: "Dedicated reserved pricing reduces per-token unit by up to 42% at X commit levels; hosted billing also offers burst protections and quotas."
  - Counter: "We can model your 12-month spend and show break-even for Dedicated vs Hosted in the pilot phase."

- Card E1 (Quick Proofs): 3 short evidence bites to use any time
  - 1-liner latency proof: "Median 3ms token path (hosted, chat-optimized)."
  - 1-liner cost proof: "Typical PLG pilot: 28% lower per-token cost using cache + smart batching."
  - 1-liner reliability proof: "Auto-fallback to validated model variants keeps application error rates stable during rolling infra events."

- Card E2 (Objection Cheats): top 6 objections and micro-scripts (each 1 line)
  - "Is it cheaper to self-host?" → "Maybe at scale; we help model the runbook and show committed vs self-host TCO with infra ops included."
  - "Will my PII leave our VPC?" → "Private option keeps control plane in your VPC, optional on-prem for air-gapped requirements."
  - "What about vendor lock-in?" → "Open model catalog + ability to pin model versions + data export make migration feasible by design."

- Card E3 (Call to Action & Pilot checklist): 6 quick entry criteria
  - 1) Business event: conversion lift or new chat surface
  - 2) 1–2 test prompts (representative)
  - 3) SLO target (p95 < 200ms typical)
  - 4) Data residency / compliance must-haves
  - 5) Stakeholders: Eng, Security, Procurement
  - 6) Pilot length: 4–8 weeks recommended

Design notes (how to format slides/cards):
- Front: 1-line hook + 1 micro-stat (big, bold)
- Back: 3 bullet proofs + 1 counter + quick link (QR to long battlecard)
- Use color band by persona: teal (Architect), amber (ML Eng), indigo (Procurement).
- Size: 85 x 55 mm (business-card) for physical laminate; for PDF export ensure legible type at 10–12pt.

Measurement plan (how sellers signal value):
- Track micro-converts: "Asked for pilot" after using kit (checkbox in Salesforce call note).
- A/B with control group (SEs with vs without laminates) for 60-day pilot win-rate lift.
- Collect 2 evidence metrics per pilot: initial latency observed, modeled vs actual cost delta.

Open questions / risks (notes to product/legal):
- Need updated hosted latency/cost benchmarks by model family — who owns? (tag: eng-serving-runtime)
- Do we need legal OK for printed customer-facing proof statements? Likely yes for named percentages.
- How to keep proofs fresh — monthly update cadence or link dynamic QR to canonical page.

Next steps / owner tasks (rough timeline):
- This week: finalize 6 card wordings (Priya) -> Circulate to Diego + Ava for factual verification (2 days).
- Week 2: Eng to provide verified latency & cost numbers (Jira GTMS-4123).
- Week 3: Design comp + PDF export + QR routing to confluence page (Ava).
- Week 4: Pilot batch: 30 sellers / SEs get digital kit; 6 field reps get printed laminates (collect feedback 2 weeks after).

Quick appendix (script snippets):
- Architect 30s script: "Most orgs find inference reliability is a bigger blocker than raw model quality — Redwood gives predictable performance primitives across hosted, dedicated and private without forcing you to operate the runtime. If latency is a hard SLO, we’ll map a Dedicated pool and run a short throughput test — we usually get stable p95 under target with caching on."
- Procurement 20s price script: "We model your 12-month peak and steady-state. For many midmarket customers, a modest Dedicated commitment plus burst on Hosted reduces unit costs while preserving flexibility — we’ll show you a break-even analysis within the pilot."

Notes to self:
- Keep language prescriptive, not aspirational. No "best-in-class" claims without data.
- Make QR target the canonical battlecard with versioning tag (RM-Field-Evidence-v2).

End of draft.
